messages:
emma (eng-releases): heads up — deploybot paused the eu-west rollout after the infra incident. holding all release slots for the next window.
ricardo (sre): confirmed, seeing elevated DB retry rates and slowstore errors. good call to pause.
deploybot: deploybot: Paused 6 scheduled rollouts in channel eng-releases. Reason: incident-2024-11-euw-db-throttle.
emma (eng-releases): timeline question — do we want to fully roll back the progressing canaries or keep them pinned and wait for ops check?
nina (platform): prefer pin + observe. rollback will trigger a bunch of churn and might reintroduce cache warmup issues.
lena (product): product note — we should avoid rollback if user-facing impact is limited. we need a PSR drafted either way.
ricardo (sre): agree with pin. we can pin the canary versions to the pre-incident image and block new promotions. if metrics recover in 30m we can resume gradual promotion.
emma (eng-releases): ok. action items: 1) nerd pin affected release groups 2) hold new deploys 3) ops to confirm recovery metrics 4) product to prepare comms.
ricardo (sre): doing step 1 now — pinning releases:
```
# pin command
releasectl pin --env eu-west --group raft-service --version 2024.11.8-canary
```
ricardo (sre): pinned raft-service @ 2024.11.8-canary, lock id lock-8932.
ops-bot: metric alert cleared for slowstore latency in eu-west at 1735678925.
nina (platform): nice, seeing tail latency dropping to baseline but a few hosts still show elevated I/O. ops, do you want a staged resume or keep full freeze for current change window?
ricardo (sre): staged resume: allow only health-checked canaries to continue in current window; block new slot allocations. emma, can you update deploybot policy?
emma (eng-releases): updating policy to 'staggered-resume' for eu-west and tagging releases with incident-2024-11-euw.
deploybot: Policy updated for env=eu-west: mode=staggered-resume, max-concurrent-canaries=2.
lena (product): I'll draft a short internal blurb for CS and a one-liner for status page if we end up prolonged.
emma (eng-releases): scheduling reschedule — moving remaining non-urgent releases out of this change window to next available slot (prefer morning UTC). please ack if you need exceptions.
ricardo (sre): exception for authz-hotfix — we should still allow a manual small patch since it addresses a client 401 regresssion, but limit to blue lane.
emma (eng-releases): acked. authz-hotfix allowed with manual approval from ricardo and nina.
nina (platform): approving manual patch for authz-hotfix once preflight checks pass.
deploybot: Note: the following releases were requeued: 5 releases -> next-window-morning-UTC. authz-hotfix remains queued for manual patch.
lena (product): can we get a brief release notes update added to the requeue so CS has context? something like: "requeued due to eu-west infra incident; some canaries pinned; authz-hotfix allowed for expedited patching."
emma (eng-releases): will add that to the release metadata.
ricardo (sre): monitoring for 45m, will update here. if anything spikes we rollback policy becomes immediate rollback and full freeze.
emma (eng-releases): thanks — I'll follow up with a quick retrospective doc after incident closes. marking thread as post-incident reschedule coordination. :white_check_mark:
